business_domain: Pharmacy benefits — medicine coverage and formulary lookup

tests.name: Generic drug (atorvastatin calcium) is shown as covered, on the drug list, with correct tier and dosage
tests.description: As a guest visitor to MyPrime who has selected the BCBS Alabama health plan and the SourceRx 1.0 Drug Guide, searching for the generic drug atorvastatin calcium should return a result card and details page that both correctly show its dosage, its 'On drug list' status, and its 'Tier 1/Preferred Generic' tier — matching data manually verified against the live site.

preconditions.description: The visitor has entered MyPrime without signing in, selected the BCBS Alabama health plan (answering the Medicare Part D prompt as configured), and applied the SourceRx 1.0 Drug Guide on the Find medicines page.

evidence.quote: Every test starts from here.

steps.description: Enter the MyPrime site as a guest (without signing in), select the configured health plan, and apply the configured drug list so the Find medicines page is ready for a search.

evidence.quote: Drives the non-signed-in entry flow: home -> "explore MyPrime without signing in" -> pick the configured health plan -> land on Find medicines with the configured drug list applied.

steps.description: Search for atorvastatin, pick the matching autocomplete suggestion, and specify the drug's strength, quantity, and frequency to add it and generate a result card.

evidence.quote: Full "add a medicine" flow in one call: search, pick suggestion, set strength/quantity/frequency, submit.

steps.description: Open the full details page for the added drug to review its dosage and drug-list coverage information in more depth.

evidence.quote: card.findElement(By.cssSelector("a.medicine-name")).click();

assertions.description: The dosage/quantity/frequency shown on the search result card for atorvastatin calcium matches the expected dosing.
assertions.failure_meaning: A member could see the wrong dosage or quantity for this generic drug on the search results, causing confusion about how the medication is dispensed.

evidence.quote: Dose info on the result card did not match expected dosage/quantity

assertions.description: The formulary/drug-list status text shown on the search result card ('On drug list, Tier 1/Preferred Generic') matches the expected value.
assertions.failure_meaning: A member would be shown the wrong coverage/tier status for this generic on the search results, potentially misleading them about its cost.

evidence.quote: Formulary status on the result card did not match expected value

assertions.description: The drug name shown on the medicine details page matches the searched-for drug (atorvastatin calcium).
assertions.failure_meaning: The details page could display the wrong drug name, undermining confidence in the lookup result.

evidence.quote: Assert.assertEquals(detailsPage.getDrugName(), expected.getExpectedName());

assertions.description: The dosage/quantity/frequency shown on the medicine details page matches the expected dosing.
assertions.failure_meaning: The details page could show incorrect dosage information, leading a member to misunderstand how much medication they will receive.

evidence.quote: Assert.assertEquals(detailsPage.getDoseInfo(), expected.getExpectedDoseInfo());

assertions.description: The details page's formulary heading confirms this generic drug is marked 'On drug list'.
assertions.failure_meaning: A member would be incorrectly told a covered generic drug is not on their drug list, potentially leading them to avoid a lower-cost, covered option.

evidence.quote: Expected this generic to be marked \"On drug list\" on the details page

assertions.description: The details page's tier heading confirms this generic is classified as 'Tier 1/Preferred Generic'.
assertions.failure_meaning: A member would be shown the wrong out-of-pocket tier for this drug, potentially affecting their cost expectations.

evidence.quote: Assert.assertEquals(detailsPage.getTierHeading(), expected.getDetailTierHeading());

assertions.description: Confirms the reference (oracle) data itself correctly flags atorvastatin calcium as being on the plan's drug list, guarding against a corrupted test fixture rather than a product defect.
assertions.failure_meaning: If this fails, the test's own reference data is inconsistent, indicating a test-fixture defect rather than an application defect.

evidence.quote: Test data sanity check: this drug should be flagged onDrugList=true

tests.name: Selected health plan is displayed on the Find medicines page
tests.description: As a guest visitor to MyPrime who selects a health plan during the pre-login plan-selection flow, the Find medicines page should clearly display that same health plan back to the visitor, confirming they are viewing coverage information for the correct plan.

preconditions.description: The visitor has entered MyPrime without signing in and selected the configured health plan via the pre-login plan-selection modal.

evidence.quote: Every test starts from here.

steps.description: Enter the MyPrime site as a guest (without signing in), select the configured health plan, and apply the configured drug list, landing on the Find medicines page.

evidence.quote: Drives the non-signed-in entry flow: home -> "explore MyPrime without signing in" -> pick the configured health plan -> land on Find medicines with the configured drug list applied.

assertions.description: The health plan banner on the Find medicines page shows the same health plan the visitor selected in the pre-login modal.
assertions.failure_meaning: A member could be shown drug coverage information for the wrong health plan without realizing it, leading to incorrect cost or coverage expectations.

evidence.quote: Find medicines page did not show the health plan selected during the guest flow

test_data.description: The health plan the guest visitor selects and expects to see echoed back on the Find medicines page.
